name: Malabo
subtitle: Malabo, capital of Equatorial Guinea: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 271,008 people live in the Malabo district (counted 2015).
Bioko island covers 2,017 km2 and, according to INEGE, was called Fernando Poo during Spanish colonisation in honour of the Portuguese navigator who discovered it in 1472.
Bioko is ringed by a coastal plain about 5 km wide, which holds three bays, one of them the bay of the port of Malabo.

parts.text: Bioko island covers 2,017 km2 and, according to INEGE, was called Fernando Poo during Spanish colonisation in honour of the Portuguese navigator who discovered it in 1472.
Bioko is ringed by a coastal plain about 5 km wide, which holds three bays, one of them the bay of the port of Malabo.
A presidential decree of January 2026 declared Ciudad de la Paz, in Djibloho province, the capital of Equatorial Guinea in place of Malabo.
Malabo is described as a city of about 300,000 people on Bioko Island, which official institutions were given a year to leave after the 2026 capital decree.
Malabo was the capital from independence from Spain in 1968 until the 2026 decree.
The British called the settlement Port Clarence and it was later named Santa Isabel in honour of the Queen of Spain.
The expansion of Malabo has deepened uneven urban planning, producing neighbourhoods with large social differences and poor connections, according to the Spanish cultural centre in the city.
INEGE's yearbook tracks air traffic at the airport of Malabo and the arrival of commercial ships at the ports of Malabo and Bata.
Rapid urban growth of Malabo, the former political capital on Bioko island, and of Bata was among the reasons cited for moving the capital.
Malabo, the capital, lies in the northern part of the island of Bioko.

parts.text: 271,008 in 2015, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Malabo district (distrito) as tabulated in the 2015 census (IV Censo General de Población y Vivienda), reproduced in the INEGE 2025 statistical yearbook; not a separate urban-agglomeration figure.

items.text: The island of Bioko, later called Fernando Poo, was discovered by a Portuguese navigator, according to INEGE.
Clarence Port, the settlement that became Malabo, was founded by William Owen on 25 December 1827.
The short-lived British occupation of Fernando Po established the town of Clarence and brought liberated Africans freed from slave ships to the island.
Spain formally asserted sovereignty over Fernando Poo under Lerena and Port Clarence was renamed Santa Isabel.
The neo-Gothic cathedral of Santa Isabel, begun in 1897, was opened to worship on 22 January 1916.
Malabo became the capital of independent Equatorial Guinea.
The Centro Cultural de España en Malabo opened its doors on 15 February 2003.
A fire destroyed the roof of the century-old cathedral while it was closed for restoration.
A presidential decree moved the capital from Malabo to Ciudad de la Paz.

blocks.q: Myth or fact: Antoni Gaudí designed or approved the cathedral of Malabo.
blocks.explain: Several publications said Gaudí advised the designer, but the Gaudí Foundation states that no known document supports any intervention by him; the monument was built between 1897 and 1916 by the Claretian missionary Luis Sagarra Llauradó.
